what: How each Washington place voted in six contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic candidate or ticket, the Republican candidate or ticket, everyone else together (write-ins included) and the total, added up from the Washington Secretary of State's official precinct results.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, in the Washington Secretary of State's official precinct results of the certified election, added up here by county, by city or town and by legislative district, on the precinct and district lines in force at that election, with the Secretary's own list of the districts each precinct lies in. Where that list divides a precinct between a city and land outside it, or between two districts, the results still give the precinct's votes whole; they are never divided by estimate, so such a place is left out for that year. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a place is not its lines for ever: where a city annexed land or a district was redrawn, the figures are for the lines of that year. Washington holds a top-two primary, in which a candidate states a party preference that the ballot prints; a preference does not mean the party nominated or endorsed the candidate (the presidential tickets are the parties' nominees). Washington elected its Governor in 2020 and 2024 and held no contest for U.S. Senator in 2020. The candidates and tickets are named, as the results name them, only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted, so there the split is left out.

few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are the official record all the same, and are kept here so that the sums can be checked.

not_given: County commissioner and council districts: in most counties the general election for commissioner is countywide, and the precinct list writes those districts too differently from county to county to be read without guessing, so they are not added up. School, fire, port, utility and other districts are not added up, and neither are city wards. Unincorporated places are not given: they are counties' land, and their figures are in the county's.

contests.office: President and Vice President of the United States
President and Vice President of the United States

mcd.why_not: A city is missing in a year when a precinct of it that cast votes lay partly outside it: the results give such a precinct whole, and nothing is divided by estimate.
mcd.note: A city or town is the precincts the Secretary's list places in its whole-city district (never its wards), matched by name to the Census Bureau's incorporated place; a city in several counties is all of them. A year is left out for a city when a precinct of it that cast votes lies partly outside it, since the results give that precinct whole.

house.what: Legislative districts of the plan first used in 2022, as redrawn for 2024 (House seats)
house.why_not: The 2020 election was held on the districts of 2012; the districts drawn after the 2020 census were first used in 2022, so 2020 is not given. A federal court's remedial map redrew some districts for 2024 (Soto Palmer v. Hobbs). A 2022 figure is given only for a district that no precinct moved into or out of between the 2022 and 2024 lists, so it is for the lines the district has today; the districts left out are listed.
house.note: Washington elects one Senator and two Representatives from each of its 49 legislative districts, so a number's House and Senate figures are the same district's. Every precinct lies in one legislative district, and a district is its precincts added up; each district was compared with the Secretary's own results by legislative district, county part by county part.
